title: Expenditure & Latency Attribution Service for Route/Model/Customer
creator: Maya Patel
description: Build a standalone backend service that deterministically attributes expenditure (GPU/token costs + infra overhead) and end-to-end latency to three primary dimensions: route, model variant, and customer (tenant). The service will consume streaming and batch telemetry (request logs, kernel-time samples, queue/dispatch delays, billing meter events) and produce time-windowed attribution slices that power Console dashboards, per-tenant bill breakdowns, and alerting for regressions. Key goals: 1) deterministic, debuggable attributions with explainable heuristics; 2) support both near-real-time (1m windows) and daily rollups; 3) bridge hosted and dedicated deployments (multi-tenant and reserved capacity) without data leakage; 4) expose an API for downstream cost queries and CSV exports for finance. This ticket covers schema design, streaming join strategy (approximate vs exact), amortization rules for shared GPU time, latency decomposition model (scheduling, kernel, queue, network), and initial implementation + QA on staging. Do not conflate this with billing invoicing; this is attribution for observability and chargeback analytics.
acceptance_criteria: Service emits time-windowed (1m and 24h) attribution records for route/model/customer with schema v1
Test harness verifies deterministic attribution for synthetic workloads (unit tests + integration test suite)
Latency decomposition fields (scheduling_ms, kernel_ms, queue_ms, net_ms, total_ms) align within 5% of sampled profilers
End-to-end pipeline handles 50k reqs/s on staging with <30s tail latency for 1m window materialization
RBAC and tenant isolation verified in private deployment smoke tests
API endpoints documented and Console can render initial per-route cost/latency tiles
tasks: Design schema for attribution records and storage layout (Parquet/ClickHouse-ready)
Prototype streaming aggregator using Flink + RocksDB for stateful joins
Implement amortization engine for shared GPU sessions (prefix/KV-aware)
Define heuristic for routing fallback attribution when model variant mismatches occur
Add unit/integration tests including adversarial timing (clock skews, out-of-order events)
Add end-to-end pipeline job in staging and create dashboards for validation
Instrument Console API endpoints to surface the new attribution records
comments: 2026-01-15 - Design review: agreed on two-tier materialization (1m streaming windows backed by 24h batch reconciliation). PM prefers deterministic attribution even if conservative; ops asked for a mode to surface fuzzy attributions for internal debugging.

2026-01-27 - Spike complete: Flink prototype can join request events with meter breaks using RocksDB keyed by session_id; memory pressure observed at 200k keyed sessions, added eviction policy and TTL heuristics.

2026-02-04 - Trade-off discussion: exact join vs approximate windowed join. Decided to use exact joins for GPU-session-level attribution and approximate (count-min) for long-tail micro-requests to keep state bounded.
2026-02-18 - Security review note: cross-tenant joins must be prevented; added tenant_id enforcement in ingest filters and validated with synthetic multi-tenant runs.
2026-02-25 - PR 2567 opened for amortization engine and unit tests. Initial review requested from @sara.kim and @benji. Highlighted need for clearer op-runbooks for state rebuilds.
2026-03-03 - QA: validated latency decomposition against sampled profiler traces for 5k requests; worst-case variance 6% on kernel_ms for long sequences—added calibration step to mapping rules.
2026-03-05 - Next steps: finalize API contract, wire dashboard tiles, schedule load test to 100k reqs/s. Due date pushed to 2026-03-20 for rollout to staging.
notes: Amortization approach: allocate shared GPU session time proportional to token contribution per request using prefix/KV deltas when available.
Failure mode: when session_id missing, fall back to route-level average per-token cost with explicit flag 'approximate_allocation' in output record.
Storage: store raw attribution slices in daily partitioned Parquet for historical reconciliation and aggregate into ClickHouse for Console queries.
Observability: provide 'explain' endpoint that returns contributing events for any attribution row to help SRE debugging.
